summary.text: David Stumbo, the Republican nominee, won the election for South Carolina attorney general on November 3, 2026, defeating Democrat Richard Hricik, and is set to take office when the new term begins. He is in his fourth term as solicitor (district attorney) for the 8th Judicial Circuit, covering four Upstate counties, and previously worked in the Attorney General's office prosecuting internet crimes against children.

paragraphs.text: Stumbo earned a bachelor's degree from Toccoa Falls College and a law degree from the University of South Carolina School of Law.
He began his prosecutorial career as an assistant solicitor in the 11th Judicial Circuit, prosecuting a wide range of criminal cases.
He then joined the South Carolina Attorney General's Office, where his work included prosecuting internet crimes against children cases and supervising the state grand jury.
Stumbo was elected solicitor of the 8th Judicial Circuit, which covers Abbeville, Greenwood, Laurens and Newberry counties, and is serving his fourth term.

He has cited more than two decades as a prosecutor, and his campaign has emphasized gun and gang violence in the Upstate and support for a bill bringing RICO-style investigative techniques to statewide grand juries.
He also proposed regional attorney general's offices around the state.
He also supports judicial reform that would have judges nominated by the governor and confirmed by legislators, as in the federal system.
Stumbo won the June 23, 2026 Republican runoff over state Sen. Stephen Goldfinch with 54.9 percent of the vote and faced Democratic nominee Richard Hricik in the November 3 general election.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 52.3% of the vote to Richard Hricik's 47.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
